purpose: Reference-quality caveat from the original acoustic signal. Preserve the frozen reference and all existing evaluation cases; this is not replacement word ground truth.

sources.relevance: The authors describe studio singing without accompaniment, initial MFA alignment, manual correction using listening and spectrograms, and additional sample-based checks. This supports provenance, not error-free or millisecond-certified labels.

publishedLabels.mappingNote: Frozen phone mapping preserves these published identities and times. JSON/TextGrid agreement establishes data consistency, not independent acoustic accuracy.

rawObservations.interpretation: Strong periodic/harmonic region inside the published non-text <AP> interval. Exact word identity is not independently certified.
A second strong periodic/harmonic region, also inside published <AP>. It is not equivalent to silence or a negligible residual.
Weaker/noisier transition before the long harmonic region; compatible with a consonantal transition, without asserting a unique phone from signal alone.
A long vowel-like region with changing structure toward its end. It can support a long vocal sound, but not by itself the claim that this sound is the separate word о.
Attenuation and noisy consonant-like transition before the sustained final vowel-like sound.
Visible entry of the final sustained harmonic region. No new exact phoneme boundary is assigned.

numericSignalMeasurements.method: Original mono PCM24 WAV at 48000 Hz, loaded as int32 and normalized by 2^31. For each reported region, subtract its mean; RMS is sqrt(mean(x^2)). Compute full autocorrelation by FFT, normalize by zero-lag energy, and report the largest value for lags corresponding to 80–500 Hz. This is descriptive periodicity, not an AI model, phone classifier or exact F0/reference-note estimator.

pairedControlComparison.observedSequence: Short vowel-like region, another short vowel-like region, a weaker/noisy transition, then a long harmonic vowel-like region occur in the same order in both recordings. Their durations differ.
pairedControlComparison.inference: The similar acoustic sequence raises the possibility that the early glissando syllables were included in <AP> and that its later stressed vowel inside походе was labelled as the separate word о. This is a reference-quality hypothesis, not independently certified replacement annotation.

candidateImplication.observableCoverageConcern: A window starting at 3.43 s skips two strong periodic regions after the preceding raw CTC word ends. Their presence is demonstrated by the raw signal; their exact lexical assignment remains uncertain.
candidateImplication.interpretation: The better first-token o peak can belong to another occurrence of an o-like vowel inside the following word. A single-token peak or reduced error against this disputed published boundary is insufficient to establish improvement. The later candidate also reduces the following word score in the provided diagnostics.
candidateImplication.parentDecision: Do not accept the late 3.43 s product change on this evidence.

conclusion.summary: The raw signal and paired-control structure cast material doubt on using the published glissando о/походе boundaries as unquestioned targets. Preserve the original reference and all 39 evaluated word occurrences, report original metrics unchanged, and attach this cautious interpretation. Independent phonetic listening/annotation is needed to certify word identities and exact replacement times.

uncertainty: The numerical periodicity confirms structured sound, not a particular phoneme or word.
The paired performance can corroborate the order of sound types, but cannot supply timestamps for another rendition.
The follow-up inspected the supplied candidate diagnostics, so its visual judgments are not a newly blinded ground-truth annotation.
Twenty-five-millisecond spectrogram windows blur short transitions; the ranges above are approximate observations rather than millisecond-certified boundaries.
A cappella provenance reduces instrumental ambiguity but does not rule out breaths, room sound or untranscribed vocal events.
